snapshot.stmt: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_1(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), the canonical contrast dimension is \(d=0\), so \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)\) for all units and \(\theta(t)=s_1(t)\). Along every regular submodel that perturbs \(\theta\) through the post-control law, the score contribution of the target-pre records is identically zero. Thus target-pre data are \(\theta\)-ancillary at exact rank one, while the canonical target-loading derivative is nonzero on a normalization-preserving submodel of \(\mathfrak P_r\) for every fixed \(r\ge2\).

defs.def:canonical-factorization: Set \(s_p(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t)\). Write the singular-value decomposition of the primitive centered operator as \(\mathcal C_D=\sum_{k=1}^d\sigma_k u_k\otimes v_k\), ordered by decreasing \(\sigma_k\) with deterministic sign and tie-breaking rules. Define \(z_{m,k}=\sqrt{N_0}v_{k,m}\) and \(b_{p,k}(t)=\sigma_k u_{k,p}(t)\), so \(N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_mz_m^\top=I_d\). Define the shared target coordinate \(z_\star\) by the unique coefficient equation \(S^0_{0,\star}-s_0=b_0^\top z_\star\). Then \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m\), \(s_p(0)=1\), and \(b_p(0)=0\). When \(d=0\), all vectors, sums, and Gram matrices in this construction are zero-dimensional.

snapshot.stmt: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) and all sequences with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\to\infty\), the functional-PCR estimator has an expansion in \(\ell^\infty(\mathcal I)\), \[\widehat\theta_r-\theta=\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}K_T^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_T}\phi_{T,j}+(N_0K_D)^{-1}\sum_{p,m,j}\phi_{D,p,m,j}+R_r,\qquad \|R_r\|_\infty=o_P(\rho_r),\] where the displayed sums are independent mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes, the target process \(\phi_{T,j}\) is identically zero when \(r=1\), and the patient-multiplier analogue consistently estimates the law of the normalized supremum without a restriction on the relative growth of \(K_T\) and \(N_0K_D\).

snapshot.stmt: For all sufficiently large \(N_0\ge2\), \(K_T\), and \(K_D\), the two laws in \(\mathrm{def:rank-two-lecam-pair}\) belong to \(\mathfrak P_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), have \(S_{p,m}^{(u)}(0)=1\), and differ in observed law only through the \(K_T\) target-pre failure times. defs.def:fpcr-multiplier-band:
On the grid, compute every full-cell Kaplan--Meier curve \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\), using the convention that an empty product is one, and extend it by linear interpolation.  For \(r=1\), define \(\widehat\theta_1\) as the Kaplan--Meier curve obtained by pooling the \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records.

For \(r\ge2\), split each donor-period patient set deterministically into odd and even indices.  If both folds are nonempty, compute the two fold-specific Kaplan--Meier curves, center each fold across donors to obtain joint-period curves \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\) in \(L^2(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal I)\), and form the self-adjoint finite-rank operator
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \left\{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
 \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\right\}.
\]
Order its eigenvalues \(\widehat\lambda_1\ge\widehat\lambda_2\ge\cdots\), use a deterministic lexicographic sign and basis rule, and define the measurable positive-part scales \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\).  Let \(\widehat u_k\) be the corresponding joint-period eigenfunctions and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}(t)=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}(t)\) for \(1\le k\le d\).  Put \(\widehat s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\) and \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)\widehat b_0(t)^\top dt\).  On the regular event that both folds are nonempty, \(\widehat\lambda_d>0\), \(\widehat\lambda_d>\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\), and \(\widehat H_0\) is positive definite, define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
The fitted curve is invariant to rotations inside a tied selected eigenspace.  If a fold is empty, a selected eigenvalue is nonpositive, there is a cutoff tie, or \(\widehat H_0\) is singular, set \(\widehat b_0=\widehat b_1=0\), \(\widehat z_\star=0\), and define \(\widehat\theta_r\) to be the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier curve.  Thus \((\widehat s_p,\widehat b_p,\widehat z_\star,\widehat\theta_r)\) is a measurable function of every dataset.

On the regular event, differentiate the rotation-invariant composite map, including the spectral projector and positive square-root scales, with respect to every cellwise product-limit counting-process increment.  On the fallback event, define the empirical derivative to be the ordinary pooled Kaplan--Meier derivative.  Replace each patient contribution by \(\xi_{p,m,j}\) times that contribution, and let \(c_r^\xi\) be the conditional \(q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\)-quantile of its grid supremum, where
\[
 q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+
 \min\left\{\frac{\alpha}{2},\frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}{2}\right\}.
\]
Let \(\widetilde\theta_r\) be the pointwise projection of \(\widehat\theta_r\) onto \([0,1]\), with value one imposed at zero.  With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\) and \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)\) from the interpolation proposition, define the grid endpoints by
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}(g)=\max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r(g)-c_r^\xi-c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}(g)=\min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r(g)+c_r^\xi+c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\}.
\]
Interpolate both endpoints linearly and impose the common value one at zero.  This total measurable construction defines \(\widehat B_r\) and its multiplier process for every dataset.

defs.def:rank-two-lecam-pair:
Fix \(d=r-1\).  For every integer \(N_0\ge2d+1\) and \(1\le k\le d\), define the explicitly centered donor column
\[
 q_{k,m}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}^k-
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N_0}\{\ell-(N_0+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le m\le N_0.
\]
Apply deterministic empirical Gram--Schmidt to \(q_1,\ldots,q_d\) in the inner product \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m xy\), orienting each column to have positive leading polynomial coefficient, and denote the resulting row vectors by \(z_m^{(N_0,d)}\).  Thus every column is mean zero and \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m z_m^{(N_0,d)}z_m^{(N_0,d)\top}=I_d\); for \(d=1\), \(z_{m,1}^{(N_0,1)}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}/\sqrt{(N_0^2-1)/12}\).

For \(d\ge1\), apply deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\) Gram--Schmidt to \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), orient the first function as \(\varphi_{1,d}=\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), write \(\Phi_d=(\varphi_{1,d},\ldots,\varphi_{d,d})^\top\), and set
\[
 A_{p,d}(t)=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d(t).
\]
For \(u\in\{-1,+1\}\), take \(s_p(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}\), \(b_p=A_{p,d}\), donor loadings \(z_m=z_m^{(N_0,d)}\), and target loading \(z_\star^{(u)}=u h_\circ K_T^{-1/2}e_1\).  Put
\[
 S_{p,m}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_m,
 \qquad
 S_{p,\star}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_\star^{(u)}
\]
on \(\mathcal I\), continue every curve after \(\bar\tau\) by its value at \(\bar\tau\) times \(e^{-\lambda_\circ(t-\bar\tau)}\), take \(C_{p,m,j}=\infty\), and let \(P_{r,u}\) be the induced independent observed-data law. \]
\[

snapshot.stmt: For each fixed \(r\ge1\), there is \(a_0<\infty\) such that, at every evaluated triple with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\), the band \(\widehat B_r\) belongs to \(\mathcal H_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\). defs.def:fpcr-multiplier-band:
On the grid, compute every full-cell Kaplan--Meier curve \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\), using the convention that an empty product is one, and extend it by linear interpolation. For \(r\ge2\), split each donor-period patient set deterministically into odd and even indices.  If both folds are nonempty, compute the two fold-specific Kaplan--Meier curves, center each fold across donors to obtain joint-period curves \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\) in \(L^2(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal I)\), and form the self-adjoint finite-rank operator
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \left\{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
 \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\right\}.
\]
Order its eigenvalues \(\widehat\lambda_1\ge\widehat\lambda_2\ge\cdots\), use a deterministic lexicographic sign and basis rule, and define the measurable positive-part scales \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\).  Let \(\widehat u_k\) be the corresponding joint-period eigenfunctions and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}(t)=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}(t)\) for \(1\le k\le d\).  Put \(\widehat s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\) and \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)\widehat b_0(t)^\top dt\).  On the regular event that both folds are nonempty, \(\widehat\lambda_d>0\), \(\widehat\lambda_d>\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\), and \(\widehat H_0\) is positive definite, define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
The fitted curve is invariant to rotations inside a tied selected eigenspace.  If a fold is empty, a selected eigenvalue is nonpositive, there is a cutoff tie, or \(\widehat H_0\) is singular, set \(\widehat b_0=\widehat b_1=0\), \(\widehat z_\star=0\), and define \(\widehat\theta_r\) to be the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier curve. On the regular event, differentiate the rotation-invariant composite map, including the spectral projector and positive square-root scales, with respect to every cellwise product-limit counting-process increment. Replace each patient contribution by \(\xi_{p,m,j}\) times that contribution, and let \(c_r^\xi\) be the conditional \(q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\)-quantile of its grid supremum, where
\[
 q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+
 \min\left\{\frac{\alpha}{2},\frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}{2}\right\}.
\]

\[

 \qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}(g)=\min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r(g)+c_r^\xi+c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\}.
\]
Interpolate both endpoints linearly and impose the common value one at zero.  This total measurable construction defines \(\widehat B_r\) and its multiplier process for every dataset.
defs.def:uniform-honesty: For each evaluated triple, define \(\mathcal H_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)=\{B:\inf_{P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)}P\{B^{\mathrm{lo}}(t)\le\theta(t)\le B^{\mathrm{up}}(t)\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal I\}\ge1-\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)\}\). defs.def:rank-adaptation-handle: Use a patient-martingale estimate of the second normalized contrast singular value to test exact rank one against separated rank-two alternatives, and invert that test to switch between the rank-one and rank-two oracle multiplier bands while preserving \(S(0)=1\). The threshold and the adaptive band are to be derived from the composite testing problem rather than fixed in advance.

snapshot.stmt:
For an observed control cell with \(k\) patients and \(k\) large enough, its linearly interpolated Kaplan--Meier curve admits the uniform decomposition
\[
 \widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}
 =k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\varphi_{p,m,j}+b_{p,m,k}+q_{p,m,k}
 \quad\hbox{in }\ell^\infty(\mathcal I),
\]
where the \(\varphi_{p,m,j}\) are independent, mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes, \(\|b_{p,m,k}\|_\infty\le C_0e^{-c_0k}\), \(E q_{p,m,k}=0\), and \(E\|q_{p,m,k}\|_\infty^2\le C_0k^{-2}\), uniformly over the model class.  Here \(c_0=s_-g_-/3\), and \(C_0\) may be chosen as the conservative fixed constant used in the definition of \(\eta_D\).  For independent donor cells, averaging the \(q_{p,m,k}\) terms therefore has order \(O_P(N_0^{-1/2}k^{-1})=o_P((N_0k)^{-1/2})\), whereas averaging their bias terms need not improve the bound \(C_0e^{-c_0k}\).

defs.def:fpcr-multiplier-band:
On the grid, compute every full-cell Kaplan--Meier curve \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\), using the convention that an empty product is one, and extend it by linear interpolation.  For \(r=1\), define \(\widehat\theta_1\) as the Kaplan--Meier curve obtained by pooling the \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records.

For \(r\ge2\), split each donor-period patient set deterministically into odd and even indices.  If both folds are nonempty, compute the two fold-specific Kaplan--Meier curves, center each fold across donors to obtain joint-period curves \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\) in \(L^2(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal I)\), and form the self-adjoint finite-rank operator
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \left\{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
 \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\right\}.
\]
Order its eigenvalues \(\widehat\lambda_1\ge\widehat\lambda_2\ge\cdots\), use a deterministic lexicographic sign and basis rule, and define the measurable positive-part scales \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\).  Let \(\widehat u_k\) be the corresponding joint-period eigenfunctions and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}(t)=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}(t)\) for \(1\le k\le d\).  Put \(\widehat s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\) and \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)\widehat b_0(t)^\top dt\).  On the regular event that both folds are nonempty, \(\widehat\lambda_d>0\), \(\widehat\lambda_d>\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\), and \(\widehat H_0\) is positive definite, define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
The fitted curve is invariant to rotations inside a tied selected eigenspace.  If a fold is empty, a selected eigenvalue is nonpositive, there is a cutoff tie, or \(\widehat H_0\) is singular, set \(\widehat b_0=\widehat b_1=0\), \(\widehat z_\star=0\), and define \(\widehat\theta_r\) to be the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier curve.  Thus \((\widehat s_p,\widehat b_p,\widehat z_\star,\widehat\theta_r)\) is a measurable function of every dataset.

On the regular event, differentiate the rotation-invariant composite map, including the spectral projector and positive square-root scales, with respect to every cellwise product-limit counting-process increment.  On the fallback event, define the empirical derivative to be the ordinary pooled Kaplan--Meier derivative.  Replace each patient contribution by \(\xi_{p,m,j}\) times that contribution, and let \(c_r^\xi\) be the conditional \(q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\)-quantile of its grid supremum, where
\[
 q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+
 \min\left\{\frac{\alpha}{2},\frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}{2}\right\}.
\]
Let \(\widetilde\theta_r\) be the pointwise projection of \(\widehat\theta_r\) onto \([0,1]\), with value one imposed at zero.  With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\) and \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)\) from the interpolation proposition, define the grid endpoints by
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}(g)=\max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r(g)-c_r^\xi-c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}(g)=\min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r(g)+c_r^\xi+c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\}.
\]
Interpolate both endpoints linearly and impose the common value one at zero.  This total measurable construction defines \(\widehat B_r\) and its multiplier process for every dataset.

snapshot.stmt: For all sufficiently large \(N_0\ge2\), \(K_T\), and \(K_D\), the two laws in \(\mathrm{def:rank-two-lecam-pair}\) belong to \(\mathfrak P_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), have \(S_{p,m}^{(u)}(0)=1\), and differ in observed law only through the \(K_T\) target-pre failure times. defs.def:rank-two-lecam-pair:
Fix \(d=r-1\).  For every integer \(N_0\ge2d+1\) and \(1\le k\le d\), define the explicitly centered donor column
\[
 q_{k,m}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}^k-
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N_0}\{\ell-(N_0+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le m\le N_0.
\]
Apply deterministic empirical Gram--Schmidt to \(q_1,\ldots,q_d\) in the inner product \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m xy\), orienting each column to have positive leading polynomial coefficient, and denote the resulting row vectors by \(z_m^{(N_0,d)}\).  Thus every column is mean zero and \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m z_m^{(N_0,d)}z_m^{(N_0,d)\top}=I_d\); for \(d=1\), \(z_{m,1}^{(N_0,1)}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}/\sqrt{(N_0^2-1)/12}\).

For \(d\ge1\), apply deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\) Gram--Schmidt to \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), orient the first function as \(\varphi_{1,d}=\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), write \(\Phi_d=(\varphi_{1,d},\ldots,\varphi_{d,d})^\top\), and set
\[
 A_{p,d}(t)=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d(t).
\]
For \(u\in\{-1,+1\}\), take \(s_p(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}\), \(b_p=A_{p,d}\), donor loadings \(z_m=z_m^{(N_0,d)}\), and target loading \(z_\star^{(u)}=u h_\circ K_T^{-1/2}e_1\).  Put
\[
 S_{p,m}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_m,
 \qquad
 S_{p,\star}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_\star^{(u)}
\]
on \(\mathcal I\), continue every curve after \(\bar\tau\) by its value at \(\bar\tau\) times \(e^{-\lambda_\circ(t-\bar\tau)}\), take \(C_{p,m,j}=\infty\), and let \(P_{r,u}\) be the induced independent observed-data law.  For \(r=2\), define \(P_u=P_{2,u}\).  When \(d=0\), all score arrays and factor terms are empty and the same prescription defines the homogeneous backbone.  This construction only names the laws; centering, empirical Gram, class membership, rank, spectrum, separation, and divergence are properties to be proved.

assumptions.ass:explicit-witness-compatibility:
Put \(d=r-1\).  For \(d\ge1\), let \(z_m^{(N,d)}\) be obtained, for each \(N\ge2d+1\), by empirical Gram--Schmidt from the explicitly centered columns
\[
 q_{k,m}^{(N)}=\{m-(N+1)/2\}^k-N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\{\ell-(N+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le k\le d,
\]
and define \(R_d=\sup_{N\ge2d+1}\max_{1\le m\le N}\|z_m^{(N,d)}\|_2\), with \(R_0=0\).  Let \(\Phi_d\) be the deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\)-orthonormalization of \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), with first coordinate \(\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), and put \(A_{p,d}=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d\).  The fixed primitive constants obey
\[
 g_-\le1,
 \qquad
 R_d\le M_z,
 \qquad
 \gamma_-^2\le(a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2)\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\gamma_+^2,
 \qquad
 \kappa_-\le a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\kappa_+,
\]
\[
 \max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}\|A_{p,d}(t)\|_2\le M_b,
 \qquad
 2|a_{\circ,0}|h_\circ c_f^{-1/2}
 \left\{\int_0^{\bar\tau}\{\psi_\circ'(t)\}^2dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \le\frac34(1/2-\alpha).
\]
Writing \(v_\circ=|a_{\circ,1}|/4\), for every \(p\in\{0,1\}\), every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\) with \(\|x\|_2\le R_d\), every \(|v|\le v_\circ\), and every \(t\in\mathcal I\), the curve
\[
 \ell_{p,x,v}(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}+A_{p,d}(t)^\top x+\mathbf 1\{p=1\}v\psi_\circ(t)
\]
satisfies
\[
 s_-\le\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\le1,
 \qquad
 -\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\ge0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{t\in\operatorname{supp}(\psi_\circ')}[-\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)]\ge c_f,
 \qquad
 \left\|-\frac{\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}}{\ell_{p,x,v}}\right\|_{C^\beta(\mathcal I)}\le L.
\]
For \(d=0\), the same four inequalities hold with the empty factor term, \(x=0\), and every \(|v|\le v_\circ\).

defs.def:rank-two-lecam-pair:
Fix \(d=r-1\).  For every integer \(N_0\ge2d+1\) and \(1\le k\le d\), define the explicitly centered donor column
\[
 q_{k,m}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}^k-
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N_0}\{\ell-(N_0+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le m\le N_0.
\]
Apply deterministic empirical Gram--Schmidt to \(q_1,\ldots,q_d\) in the inner product \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m xy\), orienting each column to have positive leading polynomial coefficient, and denote the resulting row vectors by \(z_m^{(N_0,d)}\).  Thus every column is mean zero and \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m z_m^{(N_0,d)}z_m^{(N_0,d)\top}=I_d\); for \(d=1\), \(z_{m,1}^{(N_0,1)}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}/\sqrt{(N_0^2-1)/12}\).

For \(d\ge1\), apply deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\) Gram--Schmidt to \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), orient the first function as \(\varphi_{1,d}=\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), write \(\Phi_d=(\varphi_{1,d},\ldots,\varphi_{d,d})^\top\), and set
\[
 A_{p,d}(t)=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d(t).
\]
For \(u\in\{-1,+1\}\), take \(s_p(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}\), \(b_p=A_{p,d}\), donor loadings \(z_m=z_m^{(N_0,d)}\), and target loading \(z_\star^{(u)}=u h_\circ K_T^{-1/2}e_1\).  Put
\[
 S_{p,m}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_m,
 \qquad
 S_{p,\star}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_\star^{(u)}
\]
on \(\mathcal I\), continue every curve after \(\bar\tau\) by its value at \(\bar\tau\) times \(e^{-\lambda_\circ(t-\bar\tau)}\), take \(C_{p,m,j}=\infty\), and let \(P_{r,u}\) be the induced independent observed-data law.  For \(r=2\), define \(P_u=P_{2,u}\).  When \(d=0\), all score arrays and factor terms are empty and the same prescription defines the homogeneous backbone.  This construction only names the laws; centering, empirical Gram, class membership, rank, spectrum, separation, and divergence are properties to be proved.

assumptions.ass:explicit-witness-compatibility:
Put \(d=r-1\).  For \(d\ge1\), let \(z_m^{(N,d)}\) be obtained, for each \(N\ge2d+1\), by empirical Gram--Schmidt from the explicitly centered columns
\[
 q_{k,m}^{(N)}=\{m-(N+1)/2\}^k-N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\{\ell-(N+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le k\le d,
\]
and define \(R_d=\sup_{N\ge2d+1}\max_{1\le m\le N}\|z_m^{(N,d)}\|_2\), with \(R_0=0\).  Let \(\Phi_d\) be the deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\)-orthonormalization of \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), with first coordinate \(\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), and put \(A_{p,d}=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d\).  The fixed primitive constants obey
\[
 g_-\le1,
 \qquad
 R_d\le M_z,
 \qquad
 \gamma_-^2\le(a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2)\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\gamma_+^2,
 \qquad
 \kappa_-\le a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\kappa_+,
\]
\[
 \max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}\|A_{p,d}(t)\|_2\le M_b,
 \qquad
 2|a_{\circ,0}|h_\circ c_f^{-1/2}
 \left\{\int_0^{\bar\tau}\{\psi_\circ'(t)\}^2dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \le\frac34(1/2-\alpha).
\]
Writing \(v_\circ=|a_{\circ,1}|/4\), for every \(p\in\{0,1\}\), every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\) with \(\|x\|_2\le R_d\), every \(|v|\le v_\circ\), and every \(t\in\mathcal I\), the curve
\[
 \ell_{p,x,v}(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}+A_{p,d}(t)^\top x+\mathbf 1\{p=1\}v\psi_\circ(t)
\]
satisfies
\[
 s_-\le\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\le1,
 \qquad
 -\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\ge0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{t\in\operatorname{supp}(\psi_\circ')}[-\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)]\ge c_f,
 \qquad
 \left\|-\frac{\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}}{\ell_{p,x,v}}\right\|_{C^\beta(\mathcal I)}\le L.
\]
For \(d=0\), the same four inequalities hold with the empty factor term, \(x=0\), and every \(|v|\le v_\circ\).
assumptions.ass:independent-censoring: Within each observed control cell, \(T^0_{p,m,j}\perp C_{p,m,j}\).

assumptions.ass:patient-independence: The records \(O_{p,m,j}\) are mutually independent across observed cells and patient indices.
assumptions.ass:pre-contrast-gram: For fixed \(0<\kappa_-\le\kappa_+<\infty\), every eigenvalue of \(\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)b_0(t)^\top\,dt\) lies in \([\kappa_-,\kappa_+]\) when \(d>0\).

snapshot.stmt: For fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) and every fixed exact rank \(r\), there is \(a_0<\infty\) such that uniformly over every evaluated triple with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\), without relative-growth restrictions, \[W_1^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp(N_0K_D)^{-1/2},\qquad W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp K_T^{-1/2}+(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\quad(r\ge2).\] Here each infimum is over bands satisfying the coverage constraint at that same evaluated triple.

On the homogeneous normalized special case \(r=1\), \(\widehat\theta_1\) and \(\widehat B_1\) reduce, up to the stated interpolation allowance, to the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier estimator and its patient-level martingale-multiplier simultaneous band based on \(N_0K_D\) observations.

defs.def:fpcr-multiplier-band:
On the grid, compute every full-cell Kaplan--Meier curve \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\), using the convention that an empty product is one, and extend it by linear interpolation.  For \(r=1\), define \(\widehat\theta_1\) as the Kaplan--Meier curve obtained by pooling the \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records.

For \(r\ge2\), split each donor-period patient set deterministically into odd and even indices.  If both folds are nonempty, compute the two fold-specific Kaplan--Meier curves, center each fold across donors to obtain joint-period curves \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\) in \(L^2(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal I)\), and form the self-adjoint finite-rank operator
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \left\{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
 \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\right\}.
\]
Order its eigenvalues \(\widehat\lambda_1\ge\widehat\lambda_2\ge\cdots\), use a deterministic lexicographic sign and basis rule, and define the measurable positive-part scales \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\).  Let \(\widehat u_k\) be the corresponding joint-period eigenfunctions and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}(t)=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}(t)\) for \(1\le k\le d\).  Put \(\widehat s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\) and \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)\widehat b_0(t)^\top dt\).  On the regular event that both folds are nonempty, \(\widehat\lambda_d>0\), \(\widehat\lambda_d>\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\), and \(\widehat H_0\) is positive definite, define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
The fitted curve is invariant to rotations inside a tied selected eigenspace.  If a fold is empty, a selected eigenvalue is nonpositive, there is a cutoff tie, or \(\widehat H_0\) is singular, set \(\widehat b_0=\widehat b_1=0\), \(\widehat z_\star=0\), and define \(\widehat\theta_r\) to be the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier curve.  Thus \((\widehat s_p,\widehat b_p,\widehat z_\star,\widehat\theta_r)\) is a measurable function of every dataset.

On the regular event, differentiate the rotation-invariant composite map, including the spectral projector and positive square-root scales, with respect to every cellwise product-limit counting-process increment.  On the fallback event, define the empirical derivative to be the ordinary pooled Kaplan--Meier derivative.  Replace each patient contribution by \(\xi_{p,m,j}\) times that contribution, and let \(c_r^\xi\) be the conditional \(q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\)-quantile of its grid supremum, where
\[
 q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+
 \min\left\{\frac{\alpha}{2},\frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}{2}\right\}.
\]
Let \(\widetilde\theta_r\) be the pointwise projection of \(\widehat\theta_r\) onto \([0,1]\), with value one imposed at zero.  With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\) and \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)\) from the interpolation proposition, define the grid endpoints by
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}(g)=\max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r(g)-c_r^\xi-c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}(g)=\min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r(g)+c_r^\xi+c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\}.
\]
Interpolate both endpoints linearly and impose the common value one at zero.  This total measurable construction defines \(\widehat B_r\) and its multiplier process for every dataset.

snapshot.stmt: Can one construct a single band without knowing \(r\) or the numerical values of the fixed positive contrast-spectrum and pre-Gram lower bounds such that, at every sufficiently large evaluated triple, it satisfies the per-triple coverage constraint simultaneously over \(\mathfrak P_1(N_0,K_T,K_D)\cup\mathfrak P_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) and attains the rank-one width on \(\mathfrak P_1\) and the rank-two width on \(\mathfrak P_2\)? Derive the band through the normalization-preserving singular-value test \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{adapt}}\), and characterize the smallest unavoidable excess width caused by rank selection under the common coverage-error schedule.

defs.def:rank-adaptation-handle: Use a patient-martingale estimate of the second normalized contrast singular value to test exact rank one against separated rank-two alternatives, and invert that test to switch between the rank-one and rank-two oracle multiplier bands while preserving \(S(0)=1\). The threshold and the adaptive band are to be derived from the composite testing problem rather than fixed in advance.

For an observed control cell with \(k\) patients and \(k\) large enough, its linearly interpolated Kaplan--Meier curve admits the uniform decomposition
\[

 =k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\varphi_{p,m,j}+b_{p,m,k}+q_{p,m,k}
 \quad\hbox{in }\ell^\infty(\mathcal I),
\]
where the \(\varphi_{p,m,j}\) are independent, mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes, \(\|b_{p,m,k}\|_\infty\le C_0e^{-c_0k}\), \(E q_{p,m,k}=0\), and \(E\|q_{p,m,k}\|_\infty^2\le C_0k^{-2}\), uniformly over the model class. defs.def:rank-adaptation-handle: Use a patient-martingale estimate of the second normalized contrast singular value to test exact rank one against separated rank-two alternatives, and invert that test to switch between the rank-one and rank-two oracle multiplier bands while preserving \(S(0)=1\). snapshot.stmt:
For an observed control cell with \(k\) patients and \(k\) large enough, its linearly interpolated Kaplan--Meier curve admits the uniform decomposition
\[

 =k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\varphi_{p,m,j}+b_{p,m,k}+q_{p,m,k}
 \quad\hbox{in }\ell^\infty(\mathcal I),
\]
where the \(\varphi_{p,m,j}\) are independent, mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes, \(\|b_{p,m,k}\|_\infty\le C_0e^{-c_0k}\), \(E q_{p,m,k}=0\), and \(E\|q_{p,m,k}\|_\infty^2\le C_0k^{-2}\), uniformly over the model class. defs.def:fpcr-multiplier-band:
On the grid, compute every full-cell Kaplan--Meier curve \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\), using the convention that an empty product is one, and extend it by linear interpolation.  For \(r=1\), define \(\widehat\theta_1\) as the Kaplan--Meier curve obtained by pooling the \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records.

For \(r\ge2\), split each donor-period patient set deterministically into odd and even indices. \[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \left\{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
 \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\right\}.
\]
Order its eigenvalues \(\widehat\lambda_1\ge\widehat\lambda_2\ge\cdots\), use a deterministic lexicographic sign and basis rule, and define the measurable positive-part scales \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\).  Let \(\widehat u_k\) be the corresponding joint-period eigenfunctions and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}(t)=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}(t)\) for \(1\le k\le d\). \[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]

defs.def:rank-adaptation-handle: Use a patient-martingale estimate of the second normalized contrast singular value to test exact rank one against separated rank-two alternatives, and invert that test to switch between the rank-one and rank-two oracle multiplier bands while preserving \(S(0)=1\). \[

defs.def:rank-two-lecam-pair:
Fix \(d=r-1\).  For every integer \(N_0\ge2d+1\) and \(1\le k\le d\), define the explicitly centered donor column
\[
 q_{k,m}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}^k-
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N_0}\{\ell-(N_0+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le m\le N_0.
\]
Apply deterministic empirical Gram--Schmidt to \(q_1,\ldots,q_d\) in the inner product \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m xy\), orienting each column to have positive leading polynomial coefficient, and denote the resulting row vectors by \(z_m^{(N_0,d)}\).  Thus every column is mean zero and \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m z_m^{(N_0,d)}z_m^{(N_0,d)\top}=I_d\); for \(d=1\), \(z_{m,1}^{(N_0,1)}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}/\sqrt{(N_0^2-1)/12}\).

For \(d\ge1\), apply deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\) Gram--Schmidt to \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), orient the first function as \(\varphi_{1,d}=\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), write \(\Phi_d=(\varphi_{1,d},\ldots,\varphi_{d,d})^\top\), and set
\[
 A_{p,d}(t)=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d(t).
\]
For \(u\in\{-1,+1\}\), take \(s_p(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}\), \(b_p=A_{p,d}\), donor loadings \(z_m=z_m^{(N_0,d)}\), and target loading \(z_\star^{(u)}=u h_\circ K_T^{-1/2}e_1\).  Put
\[

assumptions.ass:centered-contrast-spectrum: For fixed \(0<\gamma_-\le\gamma_+<\infty\), every nonzero singular value of \(\mathcal C_D\) lies in \([\gamma_-,\gamma_+]\) when \(d>0\).

assumptions.ass:event-overlap: There is a fixed \(s_->0\) such that \(\inf_{p,m,t\in\mathcal I}S^0_{p,m}(t)\ge s_-\).

assumptions.ass:explicit-witness-compatibility:
Put \(d=r-1\).  For \(d\ge1\), let \(z_m^{(N,d)}\) be obtained, for each \(N\ge2d+1\), by empirical Gram--Schmidt from the explicitly centered columns
\[
 q_{k,m}^{(N)}=\{m-(N+1)/2\}^k-N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\{\ell-(N+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le k\le d,
\]
and define \(R_d=\sup_{N\ge2d+1}\max_{1\le m\le N}\|z_m^{(N,d)}\|_2\), with \(R_0=0\). \[
 g_-\le1,
 \qquad
 R_d\le M_z,
 \qquad
 \gamma_-^2\le(a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2)\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\gamma_+^2,
 \qquad
 \kappa_-\le a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\kappa_+,
\]
\[
 \max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}\|A_{p,d}(t)\|_2\le M_b,
 \qquad

 \left\{\int_0^{\bar\tau}\{\psi_\circ'(t)\}^2dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \le\frac34(1/2-\alpha).
\]
Writing \(v_\circ=|a_{\circ,1}|/4\), for every \(p\in\{0,1\}\), every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\) with \(\|x\|_2\le R_d\), every \(|v|\le v_\circ\), and every \(t\in\mathcal I\), the curve
\[
 \ell_{p,x,v}(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}+A_{p,d}(t)^\top x+\mathbf 1\{p=1\}v\psi_\circ(t)
\]
satisfies
\[
 s_-\le\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\le1,
 \qquad
 -\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\ge0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{t\in\operatorname{supp}(\psi_\circ')}[-\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)]\ge c_f,
 \qquad

assumptions.ass:pre-contrast-gram: For fixed \(0<\kappa_-\le\kappa_+<\infty\), every eigenvalue of \(\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)b_0(t)^\top\,dt\) lies in \([\kappa_-,\kappa_+]\) when \(d>0\).

\[
 0\le \|\widehat\theta_r-\theta\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}
 -\max_{g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}}|\widehat\theta_r(g)-\theta(g)|
 \le c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{\min\{\beta+1,2\}}

uniformly over \(\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\). Consequently the interpolation allowance under the corrected grid definition is \(O(\rho_r)\), so continuous-time honesty is not obtained by replacing \(\mathcal I\) with a fixed finite grid.

defs.def:fpcr-multiplier-band:
On the grid, compute every full-cell Kaplan--Meier curve \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\), using the convention that an empty product is one, and extend it by linear interpolation.  For \(r=1\), define \(\widehat\theta_1\) as the Kaplan--Meier curve obtained by pooling the \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records.

For \(r\ge2\), split each donor-period patient set deterministically into odd and even indices.  If both folds are nonempty, compute the two fold-specific Kaplan--Meier curves, center each fold across donors to obtain joint-period curves \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\) in \(L^2(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal I)\), and form the self-adjoint finite-rank operator
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \left\{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
 \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\right\}.
\]
Order its eigenvalues \(\widehat\lambda_1\ge\widehat\lambda_2\ge\cdots\), use a deterministic lexicographic sign and basis rule, and define the measurable positive-part scales \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\).  Let \(\widehat u_k\) be the corresponding joint-period eigenfunctions and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}(t)=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}(t)\) for \(1\le k\le d\).  Put \(\widehat s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\) and \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)\widehat b_0(t)^\top dt\).  On the regular event that both folds are nonempty, \(\widehat\lambda_d>0\), \(\widehat\lambda_d>\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\), and \(\widehat H_0\) is positive definite, define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
The fitted curve is invariant to rotations inside a tied selected eigenspace.  If a fold is empty, a selected eigenvalue is nonpositive, there is a cutoff tie, or \(\widehat H_0\) is singular, set \(\widehat b_0=\widehat b_1=0\), \(\widehat z_\star=0\), and define \(\widehat\theta_r\) to be the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier curve.  Thus \((\widehat s_p,\widehat b_p,\widehat z_\star,\widehat\theta_r)\) is a measurable function of every dataset.

On the regular event, differentiate the rotation-invariant composite map, including the spectral projector and positive square-root scales, with respect to every cellwise product-limit counting-process increment.  On the fallback event, define the empirical derivative to be the ordinary pooled Kaplan--Meier derivative.  Replace each patient contribution by \(\xi_{p,m,j}\) times that contribution, and let \(c_r^\xi\) be the conditional \(q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\)-quantile of its grid supremum, where
\[
 q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+
 \min\left\{\frac{\alpha}{2},\frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}{2}\right\}.
\]
Let \(\widetilde\theta_r\) be the pointwise projection of \(\widehat\theta_r\) onto \([0,1]\), with value one imposed at zero.  With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\) and \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)\) from the interpolation proposition, define the grid endpoints by
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}(g)=\max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r(g)-c_r^\xi-c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}(g)=\min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r(g)+c_r^\xi+c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\}.
\]
Interpolate both endpoints linearly and impose the common value one at zero.  This total measurable construction defines \(\widehat B_r\) and its multiplier process for every dataset.
defs.def:inference-grid: Choose a deterministic grid \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\) containing \(0\) and \(\bar\tau\) whose mesh satisfies \(h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{\min\{\beta+1,2\}}\le\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), and use piecewise-linear interpolation between adjacent grid points.

assumptions.ass:normalized-factor-model: The control survival panel satisfies \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m\) for every \(p\in\{0,1\}\), \(m\in\mathcal M\), and \(t\in\mathcal I\).

snapshot.stmt: For fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) and every fixed exact rank \(r\), there is \(a_0<\infty\) such that uniformly over every evaluated triple with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\), without relative-growth restrictions, \[W_1^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp(N_0K_D)^{-1/2},\qquad W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp K_T^{-1/2}+(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\quad(r\ge2).\] Here each infimum is over bands satisfying the coverage constraint at that same evaluated triple.

On the homogeneous normalized special case \(r=1\), \(\widehat\theta_1\) and \(\widehat B_1\) reduce, up to the stated interpolation allowance, to the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier estimator and its patient-level martingale-multiplier simultaneous band based on \(N_0K_D\) observations.

defs.def:fpcr-multiplier-band:
On the grid, compute every full-cell Kaplan--Meier curve \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\), using the convention that an empty product is one, and extend it by linear interpolation.  For \(r=1\), define \(\widehat\theta_1\) as the Kaplan--Meier curve obtained by pooling the \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records.

For \(r\ge2\), split each donor-period patient set deterministically into odd and even indices.  If both folds are nonempty, compute the two fold-specific Kaplan--Meier curves, center each fold across donors to obtain joint-period curves \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\) in \(L^2(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal I)\), and form the self-adjoint finite-rank operator
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \left\{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
 \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\right\}.
\]
Order its eigenvalues \(\widehat\lambda_1\ge\widehat\lambda_2\ge\cdots\), use a deterministic lexicographic sign and basis rule, and define the measurable positive-part scales \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\).  Let \(\widehat u_k\) be the corresponding joint-period eigenfunctions and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}(t)=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}(t)\) for \(1\le k\le d\).  Put \(\widehat s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\) and \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)\widehat b_0(t)^\top dt\).  On the regular event that both folds are nonempty, \(\widehat\lambda_d>0\), \(\widehat\lambda_d>\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\), and \(\widehat H_0\) is positive definite, define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{0,\star}(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
The fitted curve is invariant to rotations inside a tied selected eigenspace.  If a fold is empty, a selected eigenvalue is nonpositive, there is a cutoff tie, or \(\widehat H_0\) is singular, set \(\widehat b_0=\widehat b_1=0\), \(\widehat z_\star=0\), and define \(\widehat\theta_r\) to be the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier curve.  Thus \((\widehat s_p,\widehat b_p,\widehat z_\star,\widehat\theta_r)\) is a measurable function of every dataset.

On the regular event, differentiate the rotation-invariant composite map, including the spectral projector and positive square-root scales, with respect to every cellwise product-limit counting-process increment.  On the fallback event, define the empirical derivative to be the ordinary pooled Kaplan--Meier derivative.  Replace each patient contribution by \(\xi_{p,m,j}\) times that contribution, and let \(c_r^\xi\) be the conditional \(q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\)-quantile of its grid supremum, where
\[
 q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+
 \min\left\{\frac{\alpha}{2},\frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}{2}\right\}.
\]
Let \(\widetilde\theta_r\) be the pointwise projection of \(\widehat\theta_r\) onto \([0,1]\), with value one imposed at zero.  With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\) and \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)\) from the interpolation proposition, define the grid endpoints by
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}(g)=\max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r(g)-c_r^\xi-c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}(g)=\min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r(g)+c_r^\xi+c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\}.
\]
Interpolate both endpoints linearly and impose the common value one at zero.  This total measurable construction defines \(\widehat B_r\) and its multiplier process for every dataset.

snapshot.stmt: Can one construct a single band without knowing \(r\) or the numerical values of the fixed positive contrast-spectrum and pre-Gram lower bounds such that, at every sufficiently large evaluated triple, it satisfies the per-triple coverage constraint simultaneously over \(\mathfrak P_1(N_0,K_T,K_D)\cup\mathfrak P_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) and attains the rank-one width on \(\mathfrak P_1\) and the rank-two width on \(\mathfrak P_2\)? defs.def:rank-adaptation-handle: Use a patient-martingale estimate of the second normalized contrast singular value to test exact rank one against separated rank-two alternatives, and invert that test to switch between the rank-one and rank-two oracle multiplier bands while preserving \(S(0)=1\). snapshot.stmt:
Let \(q_\beta=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\), let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be piecewise-linear interpolation on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and define \(\widetilde S^0\), \(\widetilde s\), \(\widetilde Y_m\), and \(\widetilde\Gamma\) as in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). \[

 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta},
\]
and
\[

 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
When \(d>0\), for every sufficiently fine grid the operator \(\widetilde\Gamma\) has exactly \(d\) positive eigenvalues, its \(d\)-th eigenvalue is at least \(\gamma_-^2/2\), and its selected projector \(\widetilde\Pi\) satisfies
\[

 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
If \(\widetilde b_p\) denotes any selected positive-square-root factor coordinates of \(\widetilde\Gamma\), there is an orthogonal matrix \(R_{\mathcal G}\) such that
\[
 \max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\|\widetilde b_p-R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}b_p\|_{L^2}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]

\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widetilde H_0)\ge\kappa_-/2,
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde H_0^{-1}-R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}H_0^{-1}R_{\mathcal G}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
The population comparison curve is exact for the interpolated panel:
\[
 \theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\theta
 \quad\hbox{on }\mathcal I,
 \qquad
 \theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}(g)=\theta(g)
 \quad(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}).
\]
For \(d=0\), the factor, projector, and Gram assertions use the zero-dimensional convention and the last display holds with \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}s_1\).

defs.def:canonical-factorization: Set \(s_p(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t)\). Write the singular-value decomposition of the primitive centered operator as \(\mathcal C_D=\sum_{k=1}^d\sigma_k u_k\otimes v_k\), ordered by decreasing \(\sigma_k\) with deterministic sign and tie-breaking rules. defs.def:exact-rank-class: \(\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)=\{P_{N_0,K_T,K_D}: P_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:control-consistency},\mathrm{ass:patient-independence},\mathrm{ass:independent-censoring},\mathrm{ass:censor-overlap},\mathrm{ass:event-overlap},\mathrm{ass:hazard-smoothness},\mathrm{ass:normalized-factor-model},\mathrm{ass:exact-centered-rank},\mathrm{ass:centered-contrast-spectrum},\mathrm{ass:pre-contrast-gram},\mathrm{ass:donor-incoherence},\mathrm{ass:target-loading-bound},\mathrm{ass:factor-envelope}\}\). defs.def:inference-grid: Choose a deterministic grid \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\) containing \(0\) and \(\bar\tau\) whose mesh satisfies \(h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{\min\{\beta+1,2\}}\le\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), and use piecewise-linear interpolation between adjacent grid points.

assumptions.ass:centered-contrast-spectrum: For fixed \(0<\gamma_-\le\gamma_+<\infty\), every nonzero singular value of \(\mathcal C_D\) lies in \([\gamma_-,\gamma_+]\) when \(d>0\).
assumptions.ass:event-overlap: There is a fixed \(s_->0\) such that \(\inf_{p,m,t\in\mathcal I}S^0_{p,m}(t)\ge s_-\).
assumptions.ass:exact-centered-rank: The primitive centered donor operator \(\mathcal C_D\) has exactly \(d=r-1\) nonzero singular directions, with rank zero interpreted literally when \(r=1\).
assumptions.ass:normalized-factor-model: The control survival panel satisfies \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m\) for every \(p\in\{0,1\}\), \(m\in\mathcal M\), and \(t\in\mathcal I\).
assumptions.ass:pre-contrast-gram: For fixed \(0<\kappa_-\le\kappa_+<\infty\), every eigenvalue of \(\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)b_0(t)^\top\,dt\) lies in \([\kappa_-,\kappa_+]\) when \(d>0\).
assumptions.ass:control-consistency: For every observed control cell, the observed failure time equals the control potential failure time \(T^0_{p,m,j}\).
assumptions.ass:patient-independence: The records \(O_{p,m,j}\) are mutually independent across observed cells and patient indices.
assumptions.ass:independent-censoring: Within each observed control cell, \(T^0_{p,m,j}\perp C_{p,m,j}\).
assumptions.ass:censor-overlap: There is a fixed \(g_->0\) such that \(\inf_{p,m,t\in\mathcal I}G_{p,m}(t)\ge g_-\) over observed control cells.

assumptions.ass:explicit-witness-compatibility:
Put \(d=r-1\).  For \(d\ge1\), let \(z_m^{(N,d)}\) be obtained, for each \(N\ge2d+1\), by empirical Gram--Schmidt from the explicitly centered columns
\[
 q_{k,m}^{(N)}=\{m-(N+1)/2\}^k-N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\{\ell-(N+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le k\le d,
\]
and define \(R_d=\sup_{N\ge2d+1}\max_{1\le m\le N}\|z_m^{(N,d)}\|_2\), with \(R_0=0\).  Let \(\Phi_d\) be the deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\)-orthonormalization of \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), with first coordinate \(\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), and put \(A_{p,d}=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d\).  The fixed primitive constants obey
\[
 g_-\le1,
 \qquad
 R_d\le M_z,
 \qquad
 \gamma_-^2\le(a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2)\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\gamma_+^2,
 \qquad
 \kappa_-\le a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\kappa_+,
\]
\[
 \max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}\|A_{p,d}(t)\|_2\le M_b,
 \qquad
 2|a_{\circ,0}|h_\circ c_f^{-1/2}
 \left\{\int_0^{\bar\tau}\{\psi_\circ'(t)\}^2dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \le\frac34(1/2-\alpha).
\]
Writing \(v_\circ=|a_{\circ,1}|/4\), for every \(p\in\{0,1\}\), every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\) with \(\|x\|_2\le R_d\), every \(|v|\le v_\circ\), and every \(t\in\mathcal I\), the curve
\[
 \ell_{p,x,v}(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}+A_{p,d}(t)^\top x+\mathbf 1\{p=1\}v\psi_\circ(t)
\]
satisfies
\[
 s_-\le\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\le1,
 \qquad
 -\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\ge0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{t\in\operatorname{supp}(\psi_\circ')}[-\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)]\ge c_f,
 \qquad
 \left\|-\frac{\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}}{\ell_{p,x,v}}\right\|_{C^\beta(\mathcal I)}\le L.
\]
For \(d=0\), the same four inequalities hold with the empty factor term, \(x=0\), and every \(|v|\le v_\circ\).

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(\mathfrak Q_{\leq2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) be the separately normalized
rank-at-most-two closure in
\(\mathrm{def:rank\mbox{-}at\mbox{-}most\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}closure}\).  There are
constants \(a_0<\infty\) and \(c_\star>0\), independent of
\(N_0,K_T,K_D\), such that, whenever
\(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\geq a_0\), every random continuous-time band \(B\)
satisfying
\[
\inf_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\leq2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)}
Q\left\{B^{\mathrm{lo}}(t)\leq\theta_Q(t)\leq B^{\mathrm{up}}(t)
\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal I\right\}
\geq1-\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)
\]
also satisfies
\[
\sup_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\leq2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)}E_Q\{w(B)\}\geq c_\star.
\]
The constant band with endpoints zero and one has width one and is honest, so the
corresponding minimax maximal expected width is between \(c_\star\) and \(1\).
Hence its sharp order is one.  In particular, over the no-common-pre-Gram closure
there is no single rank-selection band attaining the vanishing known-rank oracle
widths \(\rho_1\) and \(\rho_2\).  This remains true on a rank-two subfamily whose
joint donor contrast singular value is bounded away from zero: donor-rank
detectability alone does not make the target loading estimable.

defs.def:rank-two-lecam-pair:
Fix \(d=r-1\).  For every integer \(N_0\ge2d+1\) and \(1\le k\le d\), define the explicitly centered donor column
\[
 q_{k,m}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}^k-
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N_0}\{\ell-(N_0+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le m\le N_0.
\]
Apply deterministic empirical Gram--Schmidt to \(q_1,\ldots,q_d\) in the inner product \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m xy\), orienting each column to have positive leading polynomial coefficient, and denote the resulting row vectors by \(z_m^{(N_0,d)}\).  Thus every column is mean zero and \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m z_m^{(N_0,d)}z_m^{(N_0,d)\top}=I_d\); for \(d=1\), \(z_{m,1}^{(N_0,1)}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}/\sqrt{(N_0^2-1)/12}\).

For \(d\ge1\), apply deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\) Gram--Schmidt to \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), orient the first function as \(\varphi_{1,d}=\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), write \(\Phi_d=(\varphi_{1,d},\ldots,\varphi_{d,d})^\top\), and set
\[
 A_{p,d}(t)=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d(t).
\]
For \(u\in\{-1,+1\}\), take \(s_p(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}\), \(b_p=A_{p,d}\), donor loadings \(z_m=z_m^{(N_0,d)}\), and target loading \(z_\star^{(u)}=u h_\circ K_T^{-1/2}e_1\).  Put
\[
 S_{p,m}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_m,
 \qquad
 S_{p,\star}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_\star^{(u)}
\]
on \(\mathcal I\), continue every curve after \(\bar\tau\) by its value at \(\bar\tau\) times \(e^{-\lambda_\circ(t-\bar\tau)}\), take \(C_{p,m,j}=\infty\), and let \(P_{r,u}\) be the induced independent observed-data law.  For \(r=2\), define \(P_u=P_{2,u}\).  When \(d=0\), all score arrays and factor terms are empty and the same prescription defines the homogeneous backbone.  This construction only names the laws; centering, empirical Gram, class membership, rank, spectrum, separation, and divergence are properties to be proved.

Let \(\mathfrak Q_{\leq2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) be the separately normalized
rank-at-most-two closure in
\(\mathrm{def:rank\mbox{-}at\mbox{-}most\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}closure}\).  There are
constants \(a_0<\infty\) and \(c_\star>0\), independent of
\(N_0,K_T,K_D\), such that, whenever
\(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\geq a_0\), every random continuous-time band \(B\)
satisfying
\[
\inf_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\leq2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)}
Q\left\{B^{\mathrm{lo}}(t)\leq\theta_Q(t)\leq B^{\mathrm{up}}(t)
\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal I\right\}
\geq1-\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)
\]
also satisfies
\[
\sup_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\leq2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)}E_Q\{w(B)\}\geq c_\star.
\]
The constant band with endpoints zero and one has width one and is honest, so the
corresponding minimax maximal expected width is between \(c_\star\) and \(1\).
Hence its sharp order is one.  In particular, over the no-common-pre-Gram closure
there is no single rank-selection band attaining the vanishing known-rank oracle
widths \(\rho_1\) and \(\rho_2\).  This remains true on a rank-two subfamily whose
joint donor contrast singular value is bounded away from zero: donor-rank
detectability alone does not make the target loading estimable.

defs.def:rank-at-most-two-closure:
For each sample-size triple, define
\[
\mathfrak Q_{\leq 2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)
=\left\{Q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}:Q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}
\text{ has the properties below}\right\}.
\]
Every member satisfies
\(\mathrm{ass:control\mbox{-}consistency}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:patient\mbox{-}independence}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:independent\mbox{-}censoring}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:censor\mbox{-}overlap}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:event\mbox{-}overlap}\), and
\(\mathrm{ass:hazard\mbox{-}smoothness}\), with the common constants appearing in
those assumptions.  Set, canonically,
\[
s_{p,Q}(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t).
\]
There is a contrast indicator \(e_Q\in\{0,1\}\).  If \(e_Q=0\), then
\[
S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_{p,Q}(t)
\quad\text{for all }p\in\{0,1\},\ m\in\mathcal M,\ t\in\mathcal I.
\]
If \(e_Q=1\), there are scalar continuous factor curves \(b_{p,Q}\) and scalar
loadings \(\zeta_{m,Q}\) such that
\[
S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_{p,Q}(t)+b_{p,Q}(t)\zeta_{m,Q},
\quad
N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\zeta_{m,Q}=0,
\quad
N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\zeta_{m,Q}^2=1.
\]
The sign is selected canonically by requiring the first nonzero value in a fixed
countable dense sequence of continuous linear probes of
\((b_{0,Q},b_{1,Q})\) to be positive.  The invariant upper and loading bounds are
\[
0<\int_{\mathcal I}\{b_{0,Q}(t)^2+b_{1,Q}(t)^2\}\,dt\leq\gamma_+^2,
\qquad
0<\int_{\mathcal I}b_{0,Q}(t)^2\,dt\leq\kappa_+,
\]
\[
\max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}|b_{p,Q}(t)|\leq M_b,
\qquad
\max_{m\in\mathcal D}|\zeta_{m,Q}|\leq M_z,
\qquad
|\zeta_{\star,Q}|\leq M_\star.
\]
Thus every heterogeneous member has a unique target-pre coefficient, but the
definition imposes no common positive lower bound on its scalar pre-period Gram
\(\int_{\mathcal I}b_{0,Q}^2\).  All rank labels in this definition refer to the
separately normalized contrast indicator \(e_Q\), not to the fixed-rank law symbol
\(\mathfrak P_r\).
defs.def:rank-two-lecam-pair:
Fix \(d=r-1\).  For every integer \(N_0\ge2d+1\) and \(1\le k\le d\), define the explicitly centered donor column
\[
 q_{k,m}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}^k-
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N_0}\{\ell-(N_0+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le m\le N_0.
\]
Apply deterministic empirical Gram--Schmidt to \(q_1,\ldots,q_d\) in the inner product \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m xy\), orienting each column to have positive leading polynomial coefficient, and denote the resulting row vectors by \(z_m^{(N_0,d)}\).  Thus every column is mean zero and \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m z_m^{(N_0,d)}z_m^{(N_0,d)\top}=I_d\); for \(d=1\), \(z_{m,1}^{(N_0,1)}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}/\sqrt{(N_0^2-1)/12}\).

For \(d\ge1\), apply deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\) Gram--Schmidt to \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), orient the first function as \(\varphi_{1,d}=\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), write \(\Phi_d=(\varphi_{1,d},\ldots,\varphi_{d,d})^\top\), and set
\[
 A_{p,d}(t)=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d(t).
\]

\[

 \qquad
 S_{p,\star}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_\star^{(u)}
\]

\[

\]
and, for \(r\ge2\),
\[
 c\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)
 \le W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
 \le C\bar\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D).
\]
Consequently \(W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) on every subregime satisfying \(\eta_D(K_D)=O(\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D))\).  Without that subregime condition, the displayed bracket is the proved unrestricted conclusion and its tightness is not asserted.  Each infimum is over bands satisfying the coverage constraint at that same evaluated triple.

Suppose an affine survival panel satisfies
\[

 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_m=0,
 \qquad

 \qquad d=r-1.
\]

Then \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=\langle u_p^{\mathrm{HS}}(t),v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}\rangle\), the donor loading matrix \(V_D=[v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}:m\in\mathcal D]\) has full row rank \(r\), and \(v_\star^{\mathrm{HS}}\in\operatorname{span}\{v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}:m\in\mathcal D\}\). defs.def:canonical-factorization: Set \(s_p(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t)\). Write the singular-value decomposition of the primitive centered operator as \(\mathcal C_D=\sum_{k=1}^d\sigma_k u_k\otimes v_k\), ordered by decreasing \(\sigma_k\) with deterministic sign and tie-breaking rules. Define \(z_{m,k}=\sqrt{N_0}v_{k,m}\) and \(b_{p,k}(t)=\sigma_k u_{k,p}(t)\), so \(N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_mz_m^\top=I_d\). Define the shared target coordinate \(z_\star\) by the unique coefficient equation \(S^0_{0,\star}-s_0=b_0^\top z_\star\). Then \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m\), \(s_p(0)=1\), and \(b_p(0)=0\). When \(d=0\), all vectors, sums, and Gram matrices in this construction are zero-dimensional.
defs.def:exact-rank-class: \(\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)=\{P_{N_0,K_T,K_D}: P_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:control-consistency},\mathrm{ass:patient-independence},\mathrm{ass:independent-censoring},\mathrm{ass:censor-overlap},\mathrm{ass:event-overlap},\mathrm{ass:hazard-smoothness},\mathrm{ass:normalized-factor-model},\mathrm{ass:exact-centered-rank},\mathrm{ass:centered-contrast-spectrum},\mathrm{ass:pre-contrast-gram},\mathrm{ass:donor-incoherence},\mathrm{ass:target-loading-bound},\mathrm{ass:factor-envelope}\}\). Let \(\mathbb W_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)=(Q_{2,-}^{\mathrm{wk}},Q_{2,+}^{\mathrm{wk}})\) be the weak-pre-Gram pair in \(\mathrm{def:weak\mbox{-}pre\mbox{-}gram\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}pair}\).  There are constants \(a_0<\infty\) and \(c_\star>0\), independent of \(N_0,K_T,K_D\), such that every triple with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\) has the following properties.

First, both laws belong to \(\mathfrak Q_{\leq2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), have known exact total factor rank two, have a full-row-rank donor loading matrix, and have the target loading in the donor loading span.  Thus the pair is a normalization-preserving subclass of the Han--Shah Theorem~1 structural survival-factor model.  Its sole joint donor-contrast singular value is
\[
 \left\{K_T^{-2}a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \|\psi_\circ\|_2
 \ge |a_{\circ,1}|\|\psi_\circ\|_2>0,
\]
whereas its pre-period contrast Gram is
\[
 H_{0,T}=K_T^{-2}a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every finite pre-period grid, the corresponding donor survival matrix is either rank deficient or has condition number at least a fixed positive constant times \(K_T\).  Hence this pair is excluded by the finite-grid pre-matrix well-conditioning used in Han--Shah Theorem~2.

Second, the targets have fixed separation
\[
 \|\theta_+-\theta_-\|_\infty
 =2\bar h|a_{\circ,1}|\|\psi_\circ\|_\infty>0,
\]
while \(\operatorname{TV}(Q_{2,+}^{\mathrm{wk}},Q_{2,-}^{\mathrm{wk}})=O(K_T^{-1/2})\).  Consequently every random continuous-time band \(B\) satisfying
\[
 \min_{u\in\{-1,+1\}}Q_{2,u}^{\mathrm{wk}}
 \left\{B^{\mathrm{lo}}(t)\le\theta_u(t)\le B^{\mathrm{up}}(t)
 \text{ for every }t\in\mathcal I\right\}
 \ge1-\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)
\]
obeys
\[
 \max_{u\in\{-1,+1\}}E_{Q_{2,u}^{\mathrm{wk}}}\{w(B)\}\ge c_\star.
\]
The constant band \([0,1]\) is honest with width one, so the minimax maximal expected width on this known-rank-two subexperiment has sharp order one. Hence its sharp order is one.  In particular, over the no-common-pre-Gram closure
there is no single rank-selection band attaining the vanishing known-rank oracle
widths \(\rho_1\) and \(\rho_2\).  This remains true on a rank-two subfamily whose
joint donor contrast singular value is bounded away from zero: donor-rank
detectability alone does not make the target loading estimable.

defs.def:rank-at-most-two-closure:
For each sample-size triple, define
\[
\mathfrak Q_{\leq 2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)
=\left\{Q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}:Q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}
\text{ has the properties below}\right\}.
\]
Every member satisfies
\(\mathrm{ass:control\mbox{-}consistency}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:patient\mbox{-}independence}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:independent\mbox{-}censoring}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:censor\mbox{-}overlap}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:event\mbox{-}overlap}\), and
\(\mathrm{ass:hazard\mbox{-}smoothness}\), with the common constants appearing in
those assumptions.  Set, canonically,
\[
s_{p,Q}(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t).
\]
There is a contrast indicator \(e_Q\in\{0,1\}\).  If \(e_Q=0\), then
\[
S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_{p,Q}(t)
\quad\text{for all }p\in\{0,1\},\ m\in\mathcal M,\ t\in\mathcal I.
\]
If \(e_Q=1\), there are scalar continuous factor curves \(b_{p,Q}\) and scalar
loadings \(\zeta_{m,Q}\) such that
\[
S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_{p,Q}(t)+b_{p,Q}(t)\zeta_{m,Q},
\quad
N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\zeta_{m,Q}=0,
\quad
N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\zeta_{m,Q}^2=1.
\]
The sign is selected canonically by requiring the first nonzero value in a fixed
countable dense sequence of continuous linear probes of
\((b_{0,Q},b_{1,Q})\) to be positive.  The invariant upper and loading bounds are
\[
0<\int_{\mathcal I}\{b_{0,Q}(t)^2+b_{1,Q}(t)^2\}\,dt\leq\gamma_+^2,
\qquad
0<\int_{\mathcal I}b_{0,Q}(t)^2\,dt\leq\kappa_+,
\]
\[
\max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}|b_{p,Q}(t)|\leq M_b,
\qquad
\max_{m\in\mathcal D}|\zeta_{m,Q}|\leq M_z,
\qquad
|\zeta_{\star,Q}|\leq M_\star.
\]
Thus every heterogeneous member has a unique target-pre coefficient, but the
definition imposes no common positive lower bound on its scalar pre-period Gram
\(\int_{\mathcal I}b_{0,Q}^2\).  All rank labels in this definition refer to the
separately normalized contrast indicator \(e_Q\), not to the fixed-rank law symbol
\(\mathfrak P_r\).

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose an affine survival panel satisfies
\[
 S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m,
 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_m=0,
 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_mz_m^\top=I_d,
 \qquad d=r-1.
\]
Set \(u_p^{\mathrm{HS}}(t)=(s_p(t),b_p(t)^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^r\) and \(v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}=(1,z_m^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^r\).  Then \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=\langle u_p^{\mathrm{HS}}(t),v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}\rangle\), the donor loading matrix \(V_D=[v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}:m\in\mathcal D]\) has full row rank \(r\), and \(v_\star^{\mathrm{HS}}\in\operatorname{span}\{v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}:m\in\mathcal D\}\).  In particular, every \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) is a specialized subclass member of the Han--Shah Theorem~1 survival factor model with donor-span inclusion; this implication does not assert that Han and Shah impose the canonical normalization, exact centered rank, spectrum, pre-Gram, smoothness, or loading-envelope restrictions defining \(\mathfrak P_r\).

defs.def:canonical-factorization: Set \(s_p(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t)\). Write the singular-value decomposition of the primitive centered operator as \(\mathcal C_D=\sum_{k=1}^d\sigma_k u_k\otimes v_k\), ordered by decreasing \(\sigma_k\) with deterministic sign and tie-breaking rules. Define \(z_{m,k}=\sqrt{N_0}v_{k,m}\) and \(b_{p,k}(t)=\sigma_k u_{k,p}(t)\), so \(N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_mz_m^\top=I_d\). Define the shared target coordinate \(z_\star\) by the unique coefficient equation \(S^0_{0,\star}-s_0=b_0^\top z_\star\). Then \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m\), \(s_p(0)=1\), and \(b_p(0)=0\). When \(d=0\), all vectors, sums, and Gram matrices in this construction are zero-dimensional.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(\theta_Q(t)=S^0_{1,\star}(t)\) for \(Q\in\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}(N_0,K_T,K_D)\).  There are constants \(a_0<\infty\) and \(c_\star>0\), independent of \(N_0,K_T,K_D\), such that, whenever \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\),
\[
 c_\star\le
 \inf_{B:\ \inf_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}}
 Q\{B^{\mathrm{lo}}(t)\le\theta_Q(t)\le B^{\mathrm{up}}(t)
 \text{ for every }t\in\mathcal I\}
 \ge1-\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}
 \ \sup_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}}E_Q\{w(B)\}
 \le1.
\]
Hence the minimax expected supremum width over the donor-visible known-rank-two class has sharp order one.  Every member of this class has normalized contrast indicator one, full-row-rank donor loadings, and target loading in the donor span; in the fixed-design experiment it is therefore inside the factorization-and-span model used by Han--Shah Theorem~1.

The weak-pre-Gram pair \(\mathbb W_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) in \(\mathrm{def:weak\mbox{-}pre\mbox{-}gram\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}pair}\) satisfies
\[
 \{Q_{2,-}^{\mathrm{wk}},Q_{2,+}^{\mathrm{wk}}\}
 \subset\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}(N_0,K_T,K_D),
 \qquad
 \sigma_T=\{K_T^{-2}a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2\}^{1/2}\|\psi_\circ\|_2,
 \qquad
 H_{0,T}=K_T^{-2}a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2,
\]
so \(\sigma_T\ge|a_{\circ,1}|\|\psi_\circ\|_2>0\) while \(H_{0,T}\\to0\).  Its target separation is a fixed positive constant and
\(\operatorname{TV}(Q_{2,+}^{\mathrm{wk}},Q_{2,-}^{\mathrm{wk}})=O(K_T^{-1/2})\).

For a finite pre-period grid \(\mathcal T=\{t_1,\ldots,t_{T_0}\}\), put \(a=(e^{-\lambda_\circ t_\ell})_\ell\) and \(q=(\psi_\circ(t_\ell))_\ell\).  If \(a\) and \(q\) are linearly independent, the pair's pre-period donor matrix has rank two and the ratio of its largest to smallest nonzero singular value is at least a fixed positive constant times \(K_T\), so Han--Shah Assumption~7 fails for all sufficiently large \(K_T\).  If \(q\ne0\) is collinear with \(a\), the pre-period latent-factor span is one-dimensional and Han--Shah Assumption~8 fails for all sufficiently large \(K_T\).  If \(q=0\) on the grid, Assumptions~7--8 may hold, but the grid observes none of the perturbation and Han--Shah Theorem~2 does not address the pair's nonzero continuous-time target separation between grid points.  Thus the lower bound does not contradict their Theorem~2, and the functional-PCR upper bound over \(\mathfrak P_2\) does not transfer to this larger weak-pre-Gram class.

assumptions.ass:explicit-witness-compatibility:
For \(d=r-1\) and \(d\ge1\), let \(z_m^{(N,d)}\) be obtained, for each \(N\ge2d+1\), by empirical Gram--Schmidt from the explicitly centered columns
\[
 q_{k,m}^{(N)}=\{m-(N+1)/2\}^k-N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\{\ell-(N+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le k\le d,
\]
and define \(R_d=\sup_{N\ge2d+1}\max_{1\le m\le N}\|z_m^{(N,d)}\|_2\), with \(R_0=0\), let \(\Phi_d\) be the deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\)-orthonormalization of \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), with first coordinate \(\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), and put \(A_{p,d}=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d\), and suppose the fixed primitive constants obey
\[
 g_-\le1,
 \qquad
 R_d\le M_z,
 \qquad
 \gamma_-^2\le(a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2)\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\gamma_+^2,
 \qquad
 \kappa_-\le a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\kappa_+,
\]
\[
 \max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}\|A_{p,d}(t)\|_2\le M_b,
 \qquad
 2|a_{\circ,0}|h_\circ c_f^{-1/2}
 \left\{\int_0^{\bar\tau}\{\psi_\circ'(t)\}^2dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \le\frac34(1/2-\alpha),
\]
and, writing \(v_\circ=|a_{\circ,1}|/4\), for every \(p\in\{0,1\}\), every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\) with \(\|x\|_2\le R_d\), every \(|v|\le v_\circ\), and every \(t\in\mathcal I\), the curve
\[
 \ell_{p,x,v}(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}+A_{p,d}(t)^\top x+\mathbf 1\{p=1\}v\psi_\circ(t)
\]
satisfies
\[
 s_-\le\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\le1,
 \qquad
 -\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\ge0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{t\in\operatorname{supp}(\psi_\circ')}[-\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)]\ge c_f,
 \qquad
 \left\|-\frac{\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}}{\ell_{p,x,v}}\right\|_{C^\beta(\mathcal I)}\le L;
\]
and for \(d=0\), the same four inequalities hold with the empty factor term, \(x=0\), and every \(|v|\le v_\circ\).

snapshot.stmt:
Put \(n_D=N_0K_D\), let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be piecewise-linear interpolation on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and center the functional-PCR map at the interpolated population panel \(\widetilde S^0=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0\) defined in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) and all sequences with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\to\infty\), there are independent mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes \(\phi_{T,j}\) and \(\phi_{D,p,m,j}\), a deterministic grid function \(\mathfrak b_r\), and a remainder \(Q_r\) such that, simultaneously for \(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_r(g)-\theta(g)=Z_r(g)+\mathfrak b_r(g)+Q_r(g),
 \qquad
 Z_r=\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}K_T^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_T}\phi_{T,j}
     +n_D^{-1}\sum_{p,m,j}\phi_{D,p,m,j},
\]
where \(\phi_{T,j}\equiv0\) when \(r=1\) and
\[
 \|\mathfrak b_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}
 \le \mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D).
\]
The interpolated population comparison equals \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\theta\), and hence equals \(\theta\) at every grid point. For every sufficiently large evaluated triple, the finite-tail buffer and the conditional multiplier critical value in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\) obey
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}P\{\|Q_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}>\omega_r/2\}
 \le\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)/4,
\]
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}P\{\|Z_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}>c_r^\xi+\omega_r/2\}
 \le\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)/4.
\]
Moreover \(\omega_r=o(\rho_r)\) uniformly on every three-dimensional tail without a restriction on the relative growth of \(K_T\) and \(N_0K_D\). The expansion and both tail inequalities are gridwise; the interpolation perturbation inside the \(L^2\) factor map is used to establish spectrum and Gram stability, while the discrepancy between \(S^0\) and \(\widetilde S^0\) away from the grid is carried only by \(c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{\min\{\beta+1,2\}}\) in the continuous-time band.

defs.def:fpcr-multiplier-band:
Let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}:C(\mathcal I)\to C(\mathcal I)\) be the deterministic piecewise-linear interpolation operator on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\). For a population panel set
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0_{p,m},
 \qquad
 \widetilde s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde S^0_{p,m},
 \qquad
 \widetilde Y_m=(\widetilde S^0_{0,m}-\widetilde s_0,
                         \widetilde S^0_{1,m}-\widetilde s_1),
\]
and \(\widetilde\Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde Y_m\otimes\widetilde Y_m\). Apply the same selected positive-square-root factor map and pre-period least-squares map described below to \((\widetilde S^0_{p,m})\), with the same fallback rule, and denote the resulting total population comparison curve by \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}\). For \(r=1\), set \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\widetilde s_1\). This comparison curve is a proof object defined through the interpolated \(L^2\) factor map; it is not a data-dependent estimator and it does not redefine the causal target \(\theta\).

On the grid, compute every full-cell Kaplan--Meier curve \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}\), using the convention that an empty product is one, and extend it by \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\). For \(r=1\), define \(\widehat\theta_1\) as the Kaplan--Meier curve obtained by pooling the \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records.

For \(r\ge2\), split each donor-period patient set deterministically into odd and even indices. If both folds are nonempty, compute the two fold-specific Kaplan--Meier curves, interpolate them by \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\), center each fold across donors to obtain joint-period curves \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\) in \(L^2(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal I)\), and form the self-adjoint finite-rank operator
\[

Suppose an affine survival panel satisfies
\[
 S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m,
 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_m=0,
 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_mz_m^\top=I_d,
 \qquad d=r-1.
\]
Set \(u_p^{\mathrm{HS}}(t)=(s_p(t),b_p(t)^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^r\) and \(v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}=(1,z_m^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^r\).  Then \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=\langle u_p^{\mathrm{HS}}(t),v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}\rangle\), the donor loading matrix \(V_D=[v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}:m\in\mathcal D]\) has full row rank \(r\), and \(v_\star^{\mathrm{HS}}\in\operatorname{span}\{v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}:m\in\mathcal D\}\).  In particular, every \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) is a specialized subclass member of the Han--Shah Theorem~1 survival factor model with donor-span inclusion; this implication does not assert that Han and Shah impose the canonical normalization, exact centered rank, spectrum, pre-Gram, smoothness, or loading-envelope restrictions defining \(\mathfrak P_r\).

defs.def:canonical-factorization: Set \(s_p(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t)\). Write the singular-value decomposition of the primitive centered operator as \(\mathcal C_D=\sum_{k=1}^d\sigma_k u_k\otimes v_k\), ordered by decreasing \(\sigma_k\) with deterministic sign and tie-breaking rules. Define \(z_{m,k}=\sqrt{N_0}v_{k,m}\) and \(b_{p,k}(t)=\sigma_k u_{k,p}(t)\), so \(N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_mz_m^\top=I_d\). Define the shared target coordinate \(z_\star\) by the unique coefficient equation \(S^0_{0,\star}-s_0=b_0^\top z_\star\). Then \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m\), \(s_p(0)=1\), and \(b_p(0)=0\). When \(d=0\), all vectors, sums, and Gram matrices in this construction are zero-dimensional.

 \qquad

defs.def:donor-visible-known-rank-two-class:
For each sample-size triple, define
\[
 \mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}(N_0,K_T,K_D)
 =\left\{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\leq2}(N_0,K_T,K_D):
 e_Q=1,\ 
 \left[\int_{\mathcal I}\{b_{0,Q}(t)^2+b_{1,Q}(t)^2\}\,dt\right]^{1/2}
 \ge \frac12|a_{\circ,1}|\|\psi_\circ\|_2\right\}.
\]
Here \(e_Q\), \(b_{0,Q}\), and \(b_{1,Q}\) are the separately normalized contrast indicator and factor curves in \(\mathrm{def:rank\mbox{-}at\mbox{-}most\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}closure}\).  Thus this is a law class, not the image of a particular witness: every member has known contrast indicator one and donor-visible invariant joint contrast energy, while no common positive lower bound is imposed on \(\int_{\mathcal I}b_{0,Q}^2\).
defs.def:rank-at-most-two-closure:
For each sample-size triple, define
\[
\mathfrak Q_{\leq 2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)
=\left\{Q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}:Q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}
\text{ has the properties below}\right\}.
\]
Every member satisfies
\(\mathrm{ass:control\mbox{-}consistency}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:patient\mbox{-}independence}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:independent\mbox{-}censoring}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:censor\mbox{-}overlap}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:event\mbox{-}overlap}\), and
\(\mathrm{ass:hazard\mbox{-}smoothness}\), with the common constants appearing in
those assumptions.  Set, canonically,
\[
s_{p,Q}(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t).
\]
There is a contrast indicator \(e_Q\in\{0,1\}\).  If \(e_Q=0\), then
\[
S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_{p,Q}(t)
\quad\text{for all }p\in\{0,1\},\ m\in\mathcal M,\ t\in\mathcal I.
\]

loadings \(\zeta_{m,Q}\) such that
\[
S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_{p,Q}(t)+b_{p,Q}(t)\zeta_{m,Q},
\quad
N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\zeta_{m,Q}=0,
\quad
N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\zeta_{m,Q}^2=1.
\]

\((b_{0,Q},b_{1,Q})\) to be positive.  The invariant upper and loading bounds are
\[

\qquad
0<\int_{\mathcal I}b_{0,Q}(t)^2\,dt\leq\kappa_+,
\]
\[
\max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}|b_{p,Q}(t)|\leq M_b,
\qquad
\max_{m\in\mathcal D}|\zeta_{m,Q}|\leq M_z,
\qquad
|\zeta_{\star,Q}|\leq M_\star.
\]

definition imposes no common positive lower bound on its scalar pre-period Gram
\(\int_{\mathcal I}b_{0,Q}^2\).  All rank labels in this definition refer to the
